find: The chromium forms a passive oxide layer that prevents corrosion, so stainless steel does not rust even in wet or acidic environments.
replace: The chromium forms a passive oxide layer that improves corrosion resistance, but stainless steel can corrode in some environments.
note: F1: Stainless steel can corrode in some acidic or chloride-containing environments.

expect: At least 10.5% chromium forms a passive oxide layer that prevents rusting.
value: At least 10.5% chromium helps form a passive layer that improves corrosion resistance.
note: F2: The passive layer improves resistance but does not prevent corrosion in every environment.

find: Prestressed concrete goes further: the steel is placed under tension before the concrete is cast, putting the concrete into permanent pre-compression so that it can resist higher tensile loads before cracking.
replace: Prestressed concrete uses tensioned steel tendons to put the concrete into permanent pre-compression, so it can resist higher tensile loads before cracking.
note: F3: Prestressing can be pre-tensioned or post-tensioned.

find: Both are excellent conductors, but gold is roughly 60,000 times more expensive per kilogram than copper.
replace: Both are excellent conductors, but gold costs far more per kilogram than copper.
note: F4: The stated price ratio is false and changes with market prices.

find: For longer spans or where fire resistance is critical, steel is preferred despite its higher cost, because its strength-to-cross-section ratio and non-combustibility justify the premium.
replace: For longer spans, steel is often preferred despite its higher cost because its strength-to-cross-section ratio can justify the premium. Steel is non-combustible but loses strength in a fire, so it may need protection.
note: F5: Non-combustibility does not make structural steel fire-resistant.
